visual_anchor: MRI/CT shows an aggressive osseous lesion but no reliable imaging pattern distinguishes angiosarcoma from other sarcomas; pathology defines the entity. A catalog cleanup recommendation remains: remove this synonym from Adamantinoma.

visual_anchor: MRI of a superficial lower-extremity mass shows high T2 myxoid signal and curvilinear enhancing fascial tails.

visual_anchor: MRI typically shows a heterogeneous aggressive mass, an appearance shared by many sarcomas; histology defines the subtype.
rationale: No independently useful visual signature separates this pathology-defined sarcoma from the broader soft-tissue tumor differential.

visual_anchor: MRI may show a fusiform nerve-associated mass, but imaging overlaps benign nerve sheath tumors and other sarcomas; histology is required.
rationale: No independently useful visual signature separates this pathology-defined sarcoma from the broader soft-tissue tumor differential.

visual_anchor: Adolescent distal tibial epiphyseal fracture crosses epiphysis, physis, and metaphysis; CT axial/coronal reconstructions define Tillaux (anterolateral) versus triplane planes.
rationale: Combine the two adolescent transitional patterns under one physis-crossing ankle-fracture topic, with subtype-specific CT anatomy.

visual_anchor: US/MRI shows distended olecranon or prepatellar bursa with thick hyperemic wall, echogenic debris, and surrounding cellulitis.
rationale: The olecranon and prepatellar sites are one infection pattern; teach as a single septic bursitis topic.

visual_anchor: Pediatric forearm radiographs show torus cortical buckling or greenstick fracture with one cortex broken and the opposite cortex bowed/intact.
rationale: Torus and greenstick injuries are paired pediatric incomplete-fracture patterns and should share one page.
